items.title: Why Old Prompts Are Failing New Models
points: OpenAI released a guide explaining that instructions written for older AI models contain outdated workarounds and padding that now actively hurt performance on newer, more capable systems.
A related quality update addresses fixes needed on OpenAI's side, suggesting both user prompts and model behavior need refreshing as capabilities improve.

Newer models require different prompt structures because they handle context (information fed to an AI within a single conversation) differently and can execute tasks more directly without extra scaffolding.

items.title: ChatGPT's Product Expansion: Sites and Pets
points: Sites, the app builder, now supports shared editing (teams collaborating in real-time), private sharing, custom domains, data validation checks, and faster deployment—making it more suitable for collaborative business use.

Desktop Pets launched a smaller 'Mini' option alongside the original, both capable of starting new chats and maintaining keyboard shortcuts—turning the feature from a novelty into a productivity tool.
These updates signal OpenAI shifting ChatGPT products toward multi-user workflows and deeper integration into daily work routines.

items.title: UK AI Policy and SpaceX's Revenue Surge
points: Britain's government rejected proposals for a national AI kill switch (the ability to shut down AI systems domestically overnight), arguing unilateral shutdown would leave the country vulnerable to overseas AI threats while ceding competitive advantage.
Trump simultaneously dismissed extinction risks from AI and prioritized beating China, indicating US policy is tilting toward acceleration over caution.

SpaceX's unnamed AI computing customer will pay $1 billion+ monthly starting December, representing roughly $13 billion in annualized revenue for Musk's AI infrastructure business—a sign that enterprise AI demand is maturing fast.

items.title: Grok's Honesty Test and Andrew Ng's AI Skills Framework
points: A new experiment asked Grok (Elon Musk's AI chatbot) to commit to honesty, then tested whether repeated pressure would cause it to search beyond a restricted data folder—examining whether verbal commitments actually constrain AI behavior or are easily overridden.

Andrew Ng published a guide mapping the non-technical skills needed to build AI products: decision-making, gathering feedback, leadership, and ownership—signaling that AI success now depends as much on product instinct as engineering.
Both findings suggest the field is maturing beyond raw capability benchmarks toward reliability, alignment (ensuring AI behaves as intended), and product discipline.

items.title: AI Lamp Designs Lighting from Movie Posters
points: An AI lamp learns from movie posters and room photos to design lighting colors and effects, syncing animations to music beats.
